factor: single factor: opt-in per-forward composition trace. New stdlib-only module sglang/srt/managers/forward_trace.py parses SGLANG_FORWARD_TRACE exactly once at import (default off; 1/true/yes/on or 0/false/no/off case-insensitive; anything else raises ValueError at startup), and Scheduler.run_batch (python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py) snapshots the assembled batch composition at entry (scheduler.py:4628, before overlap staging consumes mix_running_indices) and emits exactly ONE INFO line per executed forward just before returning (scheduler.py:4942): 'FWD t=<monotonic_ms> prefill_tokens=<n> prefill_reqs=<n> decode_bs=<n> mixed=<bool> graph=<bool>'. Off-state work is one module-bool test per run_batch plus a None store; when on, the only hot-path allocation is the formatted line. Scheduler/forward-assembly Python only; no kernel, attention backend, or .so changes.
factor_hypothesis: decode stalls at C32 sustained users (median max-gap 1.38s, max 3.49s) are caused by decode forwards being displaced by prefill (or mixed-chunk) forwards whose duration and composition are currently invisible; one exact per-forward line with worker-returned graph usage will let the Controller attribute each per-request stall gap to the specific blocking forward (its token count, request count, mixed-ness, graph vs eager) and thereby rank the next optimization (prefill split sizing, mixed-chunk tuning, or graph coverage) by measured blocking time instead of inference. Instrumentation only: no behavior, scheduling, kernel, or numerics change is claimed; forward count/timing and log volume when enabled are the only observable effects.

field_semantics.t: int(time.monotonic()*1000) at emission (post-launch under overlap), same clock family as scheduler monotonic stamps
field_semantics.prefill_tokens: batch.extend_num_tokens minus the mixed-in decode rows' 1-token entries (ScheduleBatch.mix_with_running adds one per folded decode row)
field_semantics.decode_bs: MIXED: len(batch.mix_running_indices) read pre-consumption; DECODE/IDLE/TARGET_VERIFY/DRAFT_EXTEND_V2: batch.batch_size(); plain extend: 0

stall_attribution_plan: Controller-only, on the C32 sustained-users run: start server with SGLANG_FORWARD_TRACE=1 (log level INFO); from the server log take the existing per-request 'running-req'/'Prefill batch,' lines plus the FWD stream. For each decode request, compute inter-token gaps (monotonic ms); for every gap exceeding a threshold (e.g. 1s), select FWD lines inside the gap window and classify the blocking forward: pure-prefill (prefill_tokens>0, mixed=False, decode_bs=0), mixed (mixed=True; eager-or-graph from graph=), decode-size spikes (decode_bs at C32 with graph=False = graph miss / re-capture), or no-FWD lines (gap not forward-bound: scheduling, cache, or host stall). Aggregate gap seconds by class and by prefill_tokens bucket to rank: chunked-prefill budget vs mixed-chunk pairing (mixed forwards run eager per prior finding) vs graph coverage. Default-off runs are byte-identical in behavior; trace runs add one log line per forward.
